seed046.why: The fitted ML linear mixed model directly addresses the framed estimand: day_14_weight ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year), with a random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. The predictor was net_rearing_manipulation exactly as constructed (continuous −4 to +4; 0 unmanipulated), so larger values mean more experimentally added siblings (orientation: as_declared). The focal native-scale coefficient was −0.1807 g per additional sibling (SE 0.0157; t = −11.48; df_resid = 3631; p < 0.001). The analysis included chicks with observed day-14 weight and manipulation, excluding 85 of 3,720 for missing net_rearing_manipulation.

seed047.unit_estimated: OLS coefficient for net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood: negative=reduced, 0=unmanipulated, positive=enlarged; orientation=as_declared): −0.1775 g in chick day-14 mass per additional sibling; rear-nest-cluster-robust SE 0.0150 g; 95% CI [−0.207, −0.148].
seed047.why: This estimates the declared within-frame effect of experimentally manipulated sibling competition on nestling growth, on the native gram scale. Model: individual-chick day-14 weight regressed by OLS on net_rearing_manipulation, adjusting for categorical hatch_year, rear_nest_OH, and rear_nest_CS; sandwich SEs clustered by rear_nest_breed_ID. The fitted sample contained 3,594 chicks from 434 rearing nests in 2001–2003, excluding 85 observations missing net_rearing_manipulation and 41 missing rear_nest_CS. Larger predictor values mean more sibling competition, so the negative coefficient indicates lower day-14 mass with each sibling added.

seed048.unit_estimated: Within matched pair, the chick-level linear-regression coefficient for day-14 mass (grams) per one-chick increase in signed net_rearing_manipulation; cluster-robust t = -10.9421 with 135 df. The numeric coefficient and standard error/interval are not supplied in the analysis description.
seed048.why: This directly targets the within-frame effect of experimentally increased sibling competition on nestling growth. The predictor is the signed number of chicks added to the rearing brood (larger values mean more competition, so orientation is as_declared), and the outcome is day-14 chick mass. The model excludes nonrandomized unmanipulated broods, includes matched-pair fixed effects, clusters uncertainty by matched pair, and uses 2,327 chicks from 136 complete enlarged/reduced pairs. Predictor: signed net_rearing_manipulation.

seed049.unit_estimated: grams of chick day-14 mass per additional day-14 rearing-nest nestmate
seed049.why: The fitted model targets the declared within-frame effect of realized sibling competition on nestling growth. OLS used chick day-14 mass (g) as the outcome and d14_rear_nest_brood_size as one signed numeric predictor, adjusting for breeding-season year indicators and linear rearing-nest hatch date; cluster-robust uncertainty was computed by rearing nest (452 clusters). All 3,720 chicks were included, with no sex adjustment or exclusions. The focal estimate is -0.0934 g per additional nestmate (cluster-robust SE 0.0136; t = -6.861; approximate 95% CI -0.120 to -0.067; p approximately 7e-12). Predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size, constructed as the realized number of nestmates in the chick's rearing nest at day 14. Orientation: as_declared, because larger values indicate more sibling competition.
